Food is the *virāj*. Thus, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, he establishes himself in the *virāj*, which is food.
Regarding this, they say: "The *stoma* has reached the *virāj*, which is non-procreative; one should not perform the sacrifice with this."
Regarding this, they say: it is indeed procreation.
For the *virāj* is food;
from what is eaten, semen is emitted.
From semen offspring are born;
therefore, it is indeed for procreation.
Now, they also say that having made the *acchāvāka*’s portion eighteen-fold, one should make the *ārbhava* twenty-fold and the [final] twenty-one-fold.
"One should perform the Agniṣṭoma-sāman"—this is the rule.
Now, it is well known that one finds firm support at the end of the stotras when the twenty-one-fold (ekaviṃśa) stoma is used.
This, then, is the *śada*.
Āditya indeed desired: "May I transcend all evil by means of this very [offering] and ascend to the heavenly world.
He beheld this sacrifice.
He brought it;
he sacrificed with it. Thereupon, having indeed shaken off all evil, he ascended to the heavenly world.
This very one, having its evil struck away, shines.
Having indeed cast off all evil, he who knows thus ascends to the heavenly world.
Furthermore, because each single *stotriyā* verse falls away (*avaśīyate*), it is therefore called a *chandas*.
JB 2.83 |va Now follows this *punastoma*.
vb This seer, having returned, was unable to rise up because of the consumption of the *asura* food.
Death entered him—either because he had committed an offense against Mitra, or because he had eaten the food of those who hate him.
He said to Indra, "I am indeed unable to rise up.
He [Indra] perceived this sacrifice.
He brought it;
with it he caused him to sacrifice.
For him, the morning pressing was threefold, and the third pressing was threefold.
The *trivṛt* is indeed deficient; it flows out from what is deficient.
With these two *trivṛt* pressings, just as one might wash out a leather bag after having inflated it from both sides, even so did he wash away all his evil.
And from this side, indeed, he struck away that evil both upwards and downwards;
and he who knows thus strikes away the evil both upwards and downwards from this side.
He, being left here utterly exhausted, was unable to rise up.
He reflected: "How indeed might I restore this [sacrifice]?
He caused him to sacrifice again with that very same [offering];
by means of it, he restored it for him once more.
Furthermore, this is its stomatā (stoma-nature).
Its midday pressing consists of twelve [verses].
Twelve months are a year.

By means of the year itself, he again filled up his own self which had been emptied in the middle. He was as if one who had never received anything back; indeed, he was as if a young boy who has lost his teeth, yet such was his state of well-being.
If anyone should think himself a poison-swallower— having accepted what should not be accepted, or having eaten the food of one whose food should not be eaten—
he should sacrifice with this [offering]. With these two threefold pressings, he [drives away] the poison upwards from here, downwards from there, and in every direction.
Poison is cast away.
For him, the Bṛhat-sāman becomes the Pṛṣṭha-stotra.

This [world] is indeed the *rathantara*, and that [world] is the *bṛhat*. This world is, as it were, near, while that world is, as it were, far away; [this is done] for the sake of reaching out to that [far-off world].
For this [chant], the *gāra* *brahmasāman* occurs upon these verses beginning with "He who desires to release himself for strength," for the very purpose of warding off the *gara* (poison).

Regarding this, they say: "Those which were indeed the wish-fulfilling cows (*kāmadughā*), those very ones they took away by means of this sacrifice. Its morning pressing (*prātassavana*) is threefold (*trivṛt*), its third pressing is threefold, and the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*) is twelvefold.
The *savana*. The *jagatī* indeed consists of twelve syllables. The *jagatī* is cattle; cattle are the yielders of desires.
The Trivṛt is indeed Brahman.
By means of Brahman, they carried them away, having grasped them on both sides.
Of those cows, one yielded [milk] upon hearing.

They approached her on the ground. They seek her with the plow through agriculture; one [seek her] through trade; one, the Brahmin, through the life of a student; and one, the Kṣatriya, through service to the king.
Then those three which remained, they made them into the *ukthas*.
This very sacrifice is the *ukthya*;
for ever indeed is this the first of the *ukthya* sacrifices, and from that point on, the *agniṣṭomas* follow in succession.
He who desires cattle should sacrifice with this [offering].
At that time, they should indeed perform both the Bṛhat and the Rathantara [Sāmans] in it.
For cattle are indeed of two kinds.
Some [verses] belong to the *rathantara*, others to the *bṛhat*. Indeed, those animals that have teeth on one side are *rāthantara*; those that have teeth on both sides are *bārhata*.
This is for the attainment of both kinds of animals.
It is an Ukthya sacrifice; the Ukthas are indeed cattle, for the attainment of cattle.
For it, the Udvamśīya is the Acchāvāka’s chant; it is the form of all the Pṛṣṭhas, for cattle are the Pṛṣṭhas, for the attainment of cattle in their proper order. 84.
JB 2.85 |va Now these two, the Virāj and the Svarāj: the gods indeed desired, "May we obtain the Virāj as food; may we be sovereign in the Virāj, in food. |vb
"May we be firmly established," they said.
They saw this Virāj sacrifice;
they took it up.
They sacrificed with it;
from that, they indeed obtained the Virāj as food, and they were established in the Virāj, in food. He who knows thus obtains the Virāj as food and becomes established in the Virāj, in food.
That indeed is the Virāj where one does not long for the world of another;
he conquers that very [world] by means of this.
There are ten *trivṛt* stotras for it; these are three *virājs*, and two in the fifteen-fold [stoma].
That is the *virāj*.
Those four become the *virāj*s;
food is the *virāj*.
The Virāj [is used] for the attainment of food.
Its Rathantara is the Pṛṣṭha;
this earth, indeed, is the Rathantara.
This, indeed, is the Virāj.
He who grasps the greatest portion of her shines forth;
food is the Virāj.
[The verse] "virāja evānnādyasyāvaruddhyai" [is for the attainment of food].
[The verse] "tasyenduh samudram urviyā vibhāti" is the *ādiṣṭasāman* at the midday *pavamāna*;
it is the *sāman* of the earth.

In that way, they bring the *stoma* into fulfillment through its corresponding form. 85/ JB 2.86 |va They indeed desired: "Having secured the *virāj* as food, may we go to the world of sovereign rule (*svarājya*). 86/ JB 2.87 |va They saw this very *sāman*, the *vairāja*. Therefore, one should chant the *vairāja* [as the *sāman*] for one who desires the *virāj* as food. Through it, he goes to the world of the *adhirāj*. 90/ JB 2.91 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *parameṣṭhin*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *pārameṣṭhya*. They chanted it. Through it, he goes to the world of the *parameṣṭhin*. 91/ JB 2.92 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *rājān*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *rājana*. They chanted it. Through it, he goes to the world of the *rājān*. 92/ JB 2.93 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *kṣatra*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *kṣatram*. They chanted it. Through it, he goes to the world of the *kṣatra*. 93/ JB 2.94 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *viś*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *vaiśya*. They chanted it. Through it, they went to the world of the *bhūta*. Therefore, one should chant the *bhūta* [as the *sāman*] for one who desires the world of the *bhūta*. Through it, he goes to the world of the *bhūta*. 95/ JB 2.96 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *bhavya*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *bhāvya*. They chanted it. Through it, they went to the world of the *bhavya*. Therefore, one should chant the *bhāvya* [as the *sāman*] for one who desires the world of the *bhavya*. Through it, he goes to the world of the *bhavya*. 96/ JB 2.97 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *bhaviṣyat*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *bhaviṣyat*. They chanted it. Through it, they went to the world of the *bhaviṣyat*. Therefore, one should chant the *bhaviṣyat* [as the *sāman*] for one who desires the world of the *bhaviṣyat*. They saw these very *sāmans*, the *bhūta*, the *bhāvya*, and the *bhaviṣyat*. They chanted them. Through them, they went to the world of the *bhūta*, the *bhavya*, and the *bhaviṣyat*. Therefore, one should chant the *bhūta*, the *bhāvya*, and the *bhaviṣyat* [as the *sāmans*] for one who desires the world of the *bhūta*, the *bhavya*, and the *bhaviṣyat*. Through them, he goes to the world of the *bhūta*, the *bhavya*, and the *bhaviṣyat*. 98/ JB 2.99 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *triṣṭubh*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *traiṣṭubha*. They chanted it. Through it, they went to the world of the *triṣṭubh*. Therefore, one should chant the *traiṣṭubha* [as the *sāman*] for one who desires the world of the *triṣṭubh*. Through it, he goes to the world of the *triṣṭubh*. 99/ JB 2.100 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *jagatī*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *jāgata*. They chanted it. Through it, they went to the world of the *jagatī*. Therefore, one should chant the *jāgata* [as the *sāman*] for one who desires the world of the *jagatī*. Through it, he goes to the world of the *jagatī*. 100/ JB 2.101 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *anuṣṭubh*. They saw this very *sāman*, the *ānuṣṭubha*. They chanted it. Through it, they went to the world of the *anuṣṭubh*. Therefore, one should chant the *ānuṣṭubha* [as the *sāman*] for one who desires the world of the *anuṣṭubh*. Through it, he goes to the world of the *anuṣṭubh*. 101/ JB 2.102 |va They indeed desired: "May we go to the world of the *paṅkti*. They
They saw this sacrifice, the self-ruling one;
they brought it; with it they sacrificed.
Then, having indeed secured the Virāj as food, they went to the world of self-sovereignty.
He who knows this, having secured the Virāj as food, goes to the world of self-sovereignty. He is indeed self-ruling when he does not covet the world of another.
By this very means, he conquers that [world].
There are ten *trivṛt* stotras for it; these constitute three *virāj*s.
The fifteenth and the seventeenth are two;
that is the *anuṣṭubh*.
Indeed, this *anuṭubh* has attained the world of self-sovereignty among the meters.
The *anuṣṭubh* is indeed Prajāpati;
Prajāpati is indeed self-sovereignty (*svārājya*); and the *virāj* is indeed food.
Having established themselves in sovereignty and in food, they went to the world of self-sovereignty (*svārājya*).
He who knows thus, having established himself in sovereignty and in food, goes to the world of self-sovereignty.
For him, the *bṛhat* becomes the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra].
The Bṛhat is indeed yonder [heaven]; the Svārājya is indeed yonder [heaven].
By means of this, they went to that world of Svārājya.

He who knows this goes by means of this very [sāman] to that world of self-sovereignty (*svārājya*). Regarding the verse "The moon shines widely over the ocean," this *ādiṣṭasāman* does not occur in the *ārbhava-pavamāna*; rather, the *divaḥ-sāman* occurs there as having the sound *aikāra*.
For that world is, as it were, turned toward us; thus they perfect the *stoma* by means of its form.
Moreover, the reason it contains the sound "eka" is so that we do not pass beyond the heavenly worlds, turning away from them. (86)
JB 2.87 |va Now this is the *ṛṣabha* [sāman]. vb Indra indeed desired: "May I be the bull among all creatures; may I attain the state of being a bull."
He saw this sacrifice;
he took it up; with it, he sacrificed.
Then indeed that bull became the preeminent one among all creatures; he attained the state of being a bull.
He who knows this becomes a bull among his own offspring and attains the state of being a bull. For the bull is indeed prosperity (*śrī*).
He indeed attained prosperity.
The bull is indeed the king of men;
the bull is the bull among animals.
A bull for mares; a ram for goats;
a bull or a male goat for sheep.
|vo A bull is for the black antelopes; |vp a bull is for the spotted antelopes;
|vq these, indeed, are the splendors of the mouth.
He who knows thus attains prosperity.
It consists of fifteen parts;
the thunderbolt, indeed, is fifteenfold.
|vu Vajra is Indra. |vv This sacrifice belongs to Indra; it is performed with those same characteristics. |vw Its midday pressing consists of twenty-one [stotras].
That indeed is his *kakubh*. For those which are the best among these worlds are the *kakubhs*:
Agni is the *kakubh* of this world, Vāyu of the intermediate space, and Āditya of the sky.
He who knows thus becomes the one among the quarters.
The *bṛhat* is his *pṛṣṭha*;
Indra indeed is the *bṛhat*.
*vad*—the *pṛṣṭhas* are the *śrīs*. *vae*—they thus endow Indra himself with glory.
*vaf*—for these two, the *pavamānas*, there are the two *sāmans* specifically prescribed: the *ṛṣabha* for the *pāvamāna* and the *ṛṣabha* for the *vaidanvata*.
"Of yours.
By means of that form, they indeed bring the *stoma* to fulfillment.
Now this is the Vyoman.
The gods, indeed, desired: "May we become the Vyoman; may we go to the world that is the Vyoman.
They saw this sacrifice.
They brought it;
they sacrificed with it. Thereupon, indeed, they became the sky (vyoman) and went to the world of the sky.
He indeed becomes space; he goes to the world of space, who knows thus.
He is indeed space where he does not desire the world of another. By this very means, he conquers that [world].
It consists of seventeen parts.
Prajāpati indeed is seventeenfold;
Prajāpati indeed is the expanse (vyoman).
"By means of the void, may we become void; by means of the void, may we go to the world that is the void.
For him, both the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are employed;
indeed, one or the other of these two is not a void.
"Both of these, indeed, are the void (*vyoman*).
"By means of the void we shall become possessors of the void; by means of the void let us go to the world that is the void.
For him, the *ārbhava-pavamāna* chant consists of twenty-one verses, or it may be the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*.
Twelve months, five seasons, these three worlds, and yonder sun make up the twenty-onefold.
This indeed is the Void (*vyoman*); those gods who are on this side of Prajāpati are its [inhabitants].
With the thought, "By means of the Void, may we become possessors of the Void; by means of the Void, may we go to the world that is the Void," they [proceeded].
"The *arka* of the gods in the highest heaven; the gods of the *arka* in the highest heaven"—these two *ādiṣṭa-sāmans* belong to the two *pavamāna* [stotras].
By means of their form, they thus bring the *stoma* into perfection. 88.
JB 2.89 |va Now, these two [sacrifices], Udbhid and Valabhid—
one desiring offspring should sacrifice with these two. |vb.
The *trivṛt* and *pañcadaśa* *stomas* come into being; the *saptadaśas* are the steeds. These two, the deficient and the redundant, form a pair for procreation:
one is deficient, the other is redundant.
Indeed, from a pair that is neither deficient nor excessive, offspring and cattle are produced;
thus, that which brings about procreation is performed. Therefore, one who desires offspring should sacrifice with both.
Now they say: "One who desires spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) should sacrifice with these two. Of these two, one attains six *gāyatrī* verses, and the other attains six;
for the *gāyatrī* is indeed the Brahman.
These two sacrifices are perfected through the Gāyatrī.
Therefore, one who desires spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) should sacrifice with both.
Furthermore, they say that one who desires long life should likewise sacrifice with these two.
The Gāyatrī is indeed the vital breath;
these two sacrifices are perfected through the Gāyatrī.
Therefore, one who desires long life should sacrifice with both.
Now they say: "One who desires splendor should sacrifice with these two.
The Gāyatrī is indeed splendor;
those two sacrifices are thus fully accomplished through the Gāyatrī.
Therefore, one who desires splendor should sacrifice with both.
Furthermore, they say that one who desires heaven alone should sacrifice with these two.
Indeed, those six *gāyatrī* verses which there are, they are four *bṛhatī*s.
The *bṛhatī* indeed reached the heavenly world;
therefore, one who desires heaven should sacrifice with both.
Furthermore, they say that one who desires cattle should sacrifice with these two.
Those six *gāyatrīs* are indeed three *jagatīs*.
The *jagatī* is cattle;
therefore, one who desires cattle should sacrifice with both. 89.
JB 2.90 |va Those gods saw these two, Udbhid and Valabhid.
vb With those two, they rushed forward against them.
They split Vala by means of Vala itself;
they released the cattle by means of Udbhid.
This very [sacrifice] is the Valabhid, consisting of the Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa [stomas], having the Rathantara as its Sāman for the swelling [of strength] and the Brahma-sāman.
Now this [sacrifice] is the *udbhid*, having seven horses, seventeenfold, with the *Bṛhat* as its *Sāman* and the *Niṣedha* as its *Brahmasāman*.
Just as a shaft or a sharp stake, so indeed is this Trivṛt-stoma.
Just as one would strike with a shaft or a sharp stake, having driven it in with a wedge, even so [does he strike].
Thus, having pinned down Vala with this threefold hymn-form (*trivṛt-stoma*), they split it open with the fifteenfold thunderbolt (*pañcadaśa-vajra*).
Furthermore, they say: "This threefold hymn-form is indeed Agni;
this fifteenfold [hymn-form] is the thunderbolt."
"Just as one might heat a stone with fire and then break it with a hammer, even so, having heated Vala with this threefold Agni-stoma, they shattered him with the fifteenfold thunderbolt.
They stood right there, finding no way forward.
They raised it up by means of the *utsedha* (elevation) itself.
Now, this *udbhit* (the piercer) consists of the sevenfold and the seventeenfold.
Of these, those which are seven are the sevenfold animals; and those which are seventeen are that very seventeenfold [stoma].
Prajāpati.
They, beholding their father Prajāpati himself, went forth rejoicing. Having gone forth, they emitted [him] as a great [being].
The gods were afraid of their being carried away. Having raised them up with the *utsedha* and having settled them down with the *niṣedha*, they took them into themselves.
He who desires cattle should sacrifice with these two.

Verily, as one who splits the mountain peak (valabhid) breaks through strength with a piercing tool and releases the cattle, so too, having raised them up by means of elevation (utsedha), he settles them by means of settling (niṣedha); he places them within himself, he encloses cattle for himself, and he becomes possessed of many cattle. 90.
JB 2.91 |va| Now, these two, Satrājit and Pṛtanājit:
|vb| The gods and the Asuras indeed contended for a year with Prajāpati over these worlds.
Those gods desired, "May we conquer the hostile army.
They saw this sacrifice, the conqueror of armies;
they took it up.
With it they sacrificed. Thereupon they indeed conquered that army.
Because they conquered the army (*pṛtanām ajayan*), therefore the *pṛtanājita* has its name "conqueror of armies" (*pṛtanājittva*).
He who knows thus conquers the hostile enemy and rival army.
That [sacrifice] consists of twenty-four parts;
the year has twenty-four half-months.
It was precisely by means of the year that they conquered them.
For this [sacrifice], the Rathantara is the Pṛṣṭha-stotra;
for the Rathantara is indeed this [earth].
By this very means they conquered them from that world.
There are twelve stotras for it;
the year consists of twelve months.
Thus they conquered them month by month from the year.
There are twenty-four *stotra* and *śastra* hymns for that [rite];
the year consists of twenty-four half-months.
Thus, they conquered them from the year by means of half-months.
Having been conquered, they took refuge in Prajāpati, the father consisting of twenty-five, and in that world.
They desired them, thinking, "Let us conquer them completely. They saw this sacrifice, the Satrājit,
and they performed it.
They sacrificed with it;
it won for them the *sattra*.
Because they won the *sattra*, that is the *satrājita*’s nature as a winner of the *sattra*.
He who knows thus completely conquers his hateful rival.
It consists of twenty-five parts.
The year consists of twenty-four half-months.
Prajāpati is the twenty-fifth.
Thus, they won them from Saṃvatsara, from Prajāpati.
For him, there are twelve stotras.
Twelve months make a year;
thus they conquered them month by month from the year.
There are twenty-four *stotra* and *śastra* hymns for that [sacrifice].
The year consists of twenty-four half-months.
Thus, they conquered them in succession, half-month by half-month, from the year.
Then indeed the gods prospered, and the Asuras were defeated.
He prospers in himself, and his hateful rival is defeated, for one who knows thus. 92.
Now they say: Prajāpati, desiring offspring, beheld this *pṛtanājít* sacrifice. 93. va. vt.
He brought it;
with it he sacrificed.
For him, there are two hundred and eighty-eight *stotriya* verses.
That is deficient;
from the deficient comes procreation,
for she is born from two [limbs] that are lacking in the woman.
Each of those [rites] is performed for the sake of procreation.
That [sacrifice] becomes the twenty-fourth;
the year consists of twenty-four half-months.
The year is produced as the progenitor.
It has twelve stotras;
the year consists of twelve months.
The year is procreation;
thus, that procreation is performed.
It has twenty-four *stotra* and *śastra* hymns.
The year consists of twenty-four half-months;
the year is procreation. Thus, that procreation is performed in successive order.
He who knows thus is propagated with offspring and cattle. Prajāpati desired those [cows]: "May these offspring of mine be possessed of food.
He saw this Satrājit sacrifice.
He brought it; with it he sacrificed.
That [sacrifice] becomes twenty-fivefold.
The year indeed consists of twenty-four half-months;
the twenty-fifth [night] is food.
By means of that twenty-fifth [night], he bestowed food upon him.
It has three hundred stanzas;
that is the *virāj*.
The *virāj* is food; it was for this very purpose that he bestowed that food upon him.
These became his food-providing offspring.
He who might desire, "May I be propagated with many offspring and cattle; may these offspring of mine be food-providing," he should sacrifice with these two [offerings].
He indeed is born again with offspring and cattle; his offspring become possessed of food. 93.
Now these two are the Virāj and the Svarāj.
Two brothers should perform this sacrifice if they should desire:
"May one of us obtain the kingdom, and may the other obtain self-sovereignty (*svārājya*). Indeed, this [sacrifice] results in both the *virāj* and the *anuṣṭubh*.
This indeed is kingship that is the *virāj*;
and this is self-sovereignty that is the *anuṣṭubh*.
By means of the *virāj*, the younger attains kingship; by means of the *anuṣṭubh*, the elder attains the world of self-sovereignty.
For him, both the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are used.
Indeed, that which is the Rathantara is kingship;
whereas that which is the Bṛhat is self-sovereignty.
By means of the *rathantara* [sāman] alone, the younger one attains kingship;
by means of the *bṛhat*, the elder attains the world of self-sovereignty (*svarājya*).
For him, there are three *trivṛt* stotras, three *pañcadaśa* stotras, three *saptadaśa* stotras, and three [others].
Twenty-one-fold [stomas].
By means of the threefold [stomas] alone, the younger one attains kingship; by means of the fifteenfold [stomas], the elder one attains the world of self-sovereignty.
By means of the seventeenfold [stomas] alone, the younger one attains kingship; by means of the twenty-onefold [stomas], the elder one attains the world of self-sovereignty. 94.

Regarding this they say: "This sacrifice belongs only to one who has already come into being, not to one who desires to come into being; for its chant is non-procreative, and it results in the *virāj* and the *anuṣṭubh* meters."
The *virāj* is indeed like a perfected meter, like a full procreation;
the *anuṣṭubh*, however, is the end of the meters.
Regarding this, they say: "This sacrifice belongs to both—the one who has already become [successful] and the one who desires to become."

For him, these *stomas*— the ninefold (*trivṛt*), the fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*), the seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*), and the twenty-onefold (*ekaviṃśa*)— are deficient and redundant, forming pairs as procreators.
One is deficient, the other is redundant.
From a pair that is deficient or excessive, offspring and cattle are produced.
The *trivṛt* and the *pañcadaśa*—that is a productive pair.
The *saptadaśa* and the *ekaviṃśa*—that is a productive pair.
"May that which is a productive couple produce me.

Furthermore, when both the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are present, this indeed is a divine productive couple; since both the Bṛhat and Rathantara are a divine productive couple, may that which is a divine productive couple [produce me].
"May he not procreate.
By striking with this [verse], one becomes free from procreation when one attains the Virāj;
for the Virāj is indeed food.
From what is eaten, semen is emitted;
from semen, offspring are born.
Moreover, since it attains the *anuṣṭubh* meter, Prajāpati is indeed of the nature of the *anuṣṭubh*; Prajāpati is the *anuṣṭubh*.
"Procreation is he; may he procreate me.
This indeed is the introductory verse (*pratipad*) for two persons sacrificing together.
Regarding this, they say: "The two verses, 'Flow on, O foremost of speech' (*pavasva vāco agriya*) and 'Sing unto him, O men' (*upāsmai gāyatā nara*), should be made the introductory verses."
"These indeed are the *pratipad* verses for two sacrificers acting together;
moreover, both *sāmans* are performed here. Therefore, these two alone should be made the *pratipad*."

In that [sacrifice], they arrange these *sāmans*: the *gauḥ-sūkta* and *aśva-sūkta*, the *hāviṣmat* and *hāviṣkṛta*. Those two pairs of *sāmans* which are the *sāmans* for two co-sacrificers—those they perform for him on the *anuṣṭubh* verses of the *virāṭsvarāja* *ārbhava-pavamāna*.
For this sacrifice is indeed Virāj and Svarāj; they thus bring the Stoma to fulfillment. 96/ JB 2.97
Now, this is the sacrifice of the eldest (*jyeṣṭhayajña*). He who desires preeminence (*jyaiṣṭhya*) should sacrifice with this.
Indeed, this [sacrifice] results in eight sets of twenty-one [stomas].
There are twelve months, five seasons, these three worlds, and yonder sun as the twenty-first.
Indeed, he is the summit, the pre-eminence. [One should pray: "May he, who is the summit, the pre-eminence, cause me to attain the summit, the pre-eminence."
Its *pavamāna* chants are seventeenfold.
Prajāpati is indeed the seventeenfold.
Prajāpati is indeed the foremost and the preeminent.
"May he who is the foremost and the eldest lead me to the foremost and the eldest state. For him, the stotras are "possessing the north" (uttarāvant).
Thus, they cause him to attain that prosperity which possesses the north, and lead him to the heavenly world which possesses the north.
For him, the *bṛhat* becomes the *pṛṣṭha* chant.
Prosperity indeed is the *bṛhat*, and preeminence is the *bṛhat*. That which is yonder is the *bṛhat*, and that which is yonder is preeminence.
Thus they establish him in the very midst of the *śrīs* (prosperities) for preeminence.
There are twelve *stotras* for it;
twelve months are a year.
The year, indeed, is the foremost pre-eminence.
[Thinking: "May he who is the foremost pre-eminence cause me to attain the foremost pre-eminence," for him there are twenty-four *stotra* and *śastra* hymns.
Twenty-four half-months make a year.
The year, indeed, is the foremost and the preeminent.
May he who is the foremost and the preeminent cause me to attain the foremost and the preeminent.
He who is the eldest, the son of the first wife, and preeminent, he should sacrifice with this; he attains preeminence and does not fall away from preeminence.
Now this is the one with evil desires:
having sacrificed with the Full Moon oblation, he prepares a *caru* for Āditya. In that [offering], he gives a hundred-māna weight of gold; for Candramas, he gives gold in the afternoon.
In that [sacrifice], he gives gold weighing a hundred [mānas], and silver.
Thus, he performs this sacrifice during the forenoon and afternoon of that [day] and during the latter fortnight.
On the new moon day (amāvāsyā) of that [period], there is the consecration (dīkṣā), followed by the soma-pressing (sutyā).
This, indeed, is the course of the sun and the moon.
The sun and the moon desired: "May we both attain equal prosperity through an identical sacrifice;
may one of us win the day and the other win the night."
The two of them saw this sacrifice;
they took it up; with it, they sacrificed.
Then indeed, by means of that same sacrifice, those two attained equal prosperity.
One of them conquered the day, and the other the night.
This, indeed, is their common prosperity, in that they both sacrifice in the same world during the forenoon and the afternoon.

The forenoon is indeed the day and the afternoon is the night; [he sacrifices thus] for the conquest of both day and night. He sacrifices during the first half of the month and the second half of the month;
the first half of the month is indeed the day and the second half of the month is the night; [he sacrifices thus] for the conquest of both day and night.
There are two [cups] worth a hundred [coins].
A man indeed has a lifespan of a hundred years, a hundred senses, and a hundredfold vigor; it is for the attainment of that very sense and vigor.
The seventeenfold hymn-form (*saptadaśa-stoma*) occurs;
Prajāpati, indeed, is seventeenfold.
Prajāpati is the leader to the heavenly world.
[Thinking] "May he lead me to the heavenly world," one should offer him;
for him, there are a hundred oxen as the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
A man indeed has a lifespan of a hundred years, a hundred faculties, and a hundredfold vigor; it is for the sake of securing that very faculty and vigor [that these are performed].
All [the fires] become carriers (*vahni*);
for by means of the carrier, one goes to wherever one desires to go.

|vi All [the gifts] become boons. |vj Heaven is indeed like a boon; it is for the prosperity of the heavenly world itself. |vk One person might give this, while another might give seventeen *niṣkas* at each hymn of praise (*stotra*).
The gods and the asuras contended at the sacrifice.
Whatever the gods did at the sacrifice, the asuras did exactly that after them.
The gods said, "Whatever we do at the sacrifice, the asuras imitate us in that very thing."
"Come, let us worship with gold and Soma.
Now, at that time, gold was indeed among the gods, but not among the Asuras.
The gold of the Asuras had been seized by the gods.
They sacrificed with gold and Soma. At each hymn of praise, they gave away seventeen gold coins (*niṣkas*).
Because of that, the Asuras could not overcome them.
They said, "Alas, the gods have committed a bad hope! That indeed is the nature of a bad hope.
Then, indeed, the gods prospered and the Asuras were defeated.
He prospers in himself, and his hateful rival is defeated, for one who knows thus.
For him, the *śukra* and *candra* *sāmans* are prescribed for the two *pavamāna* [stotras].
For this sacrifice belongs to the Sun and the Moon.
Or rather, they thus perfect the *stoma* by means of its form.
Now, this is the *apaciti*.
Prajāpati created offspring. Once they were created, they did not pay him honor. He desired, "May I receive honor among these offspring."
He saw this sacrifice;
he took it up; with it, he sacrificed.
Then indeed they honored him.
But the gods did not honor Indra.
He ran to Prajāpati, saying, "The gods truly do not honor me."
He prepared this sacrifice as an act of worship for him;
he brought it; he sacrificed with it.
Then indeed the gods honored him.
But as for Darbha Śātānīka, although he was the king of the Pañcālas, they did not honor him;
even the boys used to call out to him, "Darbha! Darbha!"
Now, there were two Brahmins belonging to him: Ahīna Āśvatthi and Keśin Sātyakāmi.
They approached him, and he sat down reflecting.
They both said to him:
"What is it that the king is reflecting upon?
He replied: "Indeed, I have nothing to reflect upon. (The same expression occurs at 2.12.2 [212.13ff]).
"The Pañcālas do not show respect to me even though I am their king; they address me as 'Darbha, Darbha,' as if I were a mere boy. Therefore, I shall meditate upon this very thing."
They said to him, "This sacrificial rite is indeed called 'Apaciti' (Honoring); let us perform that sacrifice for you. "So be it," he replied.
And so they performed that sacrifice for him.
He showed them such honor that even now the Pañcālas call darbha grass "kuśa. 100.
Indeed, for this very [Soma], the Gāyatrī metre becomes the morning pressing, the Triṣṭubh the midday pressing,
and the Jagatī the third pressing. Now, in that the Gāyatrī becomes the morning pressing— the Gāyatrī has eight syllables, and there are eight Vasus.

By means of the Gāyatrī metre itself, Prajāpati and Indra attained a preeminent position among the Vasu gods at the morning pressing. Now, as for the fact that the midday pressing coincides with the Triṣṭubh— the Triṣṭubh consists of eleven syllables.

There are eleven Rudras; by means of that very metre, the Triṣṭubh, Prajāpati and Indra attained preeminence among the gods, the Rudras, at the midday pressing. Now, as for the fact that the Jagatī is associated with the third pressing: the Jagatī has twelve syllables, and there are twelve Ādityas.
By means of that very metre, the Jagatī, Prajāpati and Indra attained preeminence among the Āditya gods at the third pressing. The Gāyatrī consists of eight syllables.
The *triṣṭubh* has eleven syllables;
the *jagatī* has twelve syllables;
"vāc" is the *nidhana* of the *yajñāyajñīya*.
|vi That [verse] consists of thirty-two [syllables].
|vj Anuṣṭubh consists of thirty-two syllables.
|vk Anuṣṭubh belongs to the Viśvedevas.
By means of the *anuṣṭubh* metre alone, Prajāpati and Indra attained preeminence among all the gods at the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*).
So many indeed are the gods.
So many are the classes of gods;
it was within them alone that those two found honor.
The Brāhmaṇa is indeed of the Gāyatrī nature; the Rājanya is of the Triṣṭubh nature; the Vaiśya is of the Jagatī nature.

The Śūdra is of the *ānuṣṭubh* metre. Now, in that the morning pressing (*prātassavana*) corresponds to the *gāyatrī*, it is by means of that very *gāyatrī* metre that Darbha Śātānīka attained honor among men as a Brāhmaṇa.
Now, in that the midday pressing becomes the *triṣṭubh*, by means of that *triṣṭubh* metre,
Darbha Śātānīka attained honor among the Rājanya and among men.
Now, in that the third pressing becomes the *jagatī*, by means of that *jagatī* metre, Darbha [attained honor].
Śātānīka attained honor among the Vaiśya class of men.
The Gāyatrī has eight syllables;
the Triṣṭubh has eleven syllables.
The *jagatī* consists of twelve syllables.
"Speech" (*vāc*) is the *nidhana* of the *yajñāyajñīya*.
That makes thirty-two.
The *anuṣṭubh* consists of thirty-two syllables.
The *śūdra* is connected to the *anuṣṭubh*.
By means of that very *chandas*, the *darbha* Śātānīka attained honor among the *śūdra* people.
So many indeed are human beings;
so many are the human races.
Upon them alone did that [offering] attain its due honor. 102.
JB 2.103 |va They say: "What is the support of this sacrifice? What is its adjustment? vb He should reply: "That which does not come together from one pressing to the next."
"That which becomes an unequal pressing—that indeed is the support of this sacrifice, that is its honor," they say.
Regarding that, they say the opening verse (*pratipad*) should be performed with "davidyutatyā ruce.
For this opening verse is possessed of a multitude and is multiform.
"Indeed, the hosts attend upon him who attains glory.
Regarding this, they also say: "Flow on as the foremost of speech; sing unto him, O men"—these two indeed should be made the introductory verses (*pratipad*).
These two *pratipad* verses are indeed the many-formed *gaṇinīs*;
for here both *sāmans* are performed. Therefore, these two alone should be made the *pratipads*.
The *bṛhat* and *rathantara* [sāmans] are used. Indeed, the *rathantara* is the Brahman, and the *bṛhat* is the Kṣatra;
these two are the forms of the Brahman and the Kṣatra when they have been diminished.
May you two be auspicious and prosperous.
For by means of the auspicious, the gods became auspicious, and by means of the prosperous, they attained glory. May you two be together with great power.
By means of *sahas* (force), the gods indeed overcame the Asuras;
by means of *mahaḥ* (greatness), they became great;
*bhargas* (splendor) and *yaśas* (fame) come to be.
By *bhargas* (splendor), the gods indeed became *bhargas*;
by *yaśas* (glory), they attained glory. There are two elevations and depressions.
By means of the *utsedha*, the gods indeed performed the *autsedhya*;
by means of the *niṣedha*, they performed the *niṣedhya*. There are both the *sadoviśīya* and the *viśoviśīya*.
By means of the *viśoviśīya*, the gods settled among the people (*viś*).
By means of the *viśoviśīya*, the kings became rulers over each people.
You two become the upholders of the law and the upholders of the non-law.
By means of *dharma*, the gods indeed became *dharma*;
by means of *vidharma*, they struck down *vidharma*. In that [context], these two kinds of *dvipadā* verses in *aticchandas* meter are employed—both the longest and the shortest.
The meters. The meters are indeed cattle.
Therefore, both kinds of cattle—those that are largest and those that are smallest—attend upon what has come into being.
Indeed, both kinds of cattle—both the largest and the smallest—attend upon him who knows this.
A chariot drawn by four horses is its sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
All the horses are of the *śatakriya* breed.

*Vak*: That Rukmin Prāvepī is radiant with all his ornaments. *Val*: His chariot-covering is made of tiger-skin; his quiver is made of leopard-skin, and his side-quiver is made of bear-skin. *Vam*: The one who mounts it is clad in rhinoceros-hide armor; he is fully equipped, as is his charioteer, and they are both well-protected.
By means of the two *pratihita*s.
The charioteer (*saṃgrahītṛ*) wears golden ornaments and a garland.
This, indeed, is the form of brilliance; this is the form of honor.

In that [rite], he gives this wealth as an honorarium (*apacitam*). [He thinks: "I give wealth as an honorarium to those who have honored me. Thus, they bring the *stoma* into harmony with its corresponding form. 103.
JB 2.104 |va Now these two, Abhibhū and Vinutti.
vb The gods and the Asuras contended.
Those gods desired, "May we become superior to these Asuras.
They saw this sacrifice, the *abhibhū* (the overcoming one),
and they performed it.
With it they sacrificed; with it they overcame the Asuras. Because they overcame [them], that is the origin of the Abhibhūs and their quality of being "overcomers."
Indeed, he overcomes his hateful rival who knows thus.
On both sides of it are two *trivṛt* [stomas];
the *trivṛt* is indeed the Brahman.

By means of the Brahman, they indeed overcame them; he who knows thus overcomes his hateful rival by means of the Brahman alone. Having been defeated, they took refuge with their father Prajāpati, the thirty-three [gods].
Just as one might desire to go around in the eldest and most excellent city, so they desired those [cows], thinking, "Let us drive them away.
They saw this sacrifice, the *vinutti*.
They brought it; they sacrificed with it;
then they drove them away.
That which they pushed away (vy-anudanta) is the reason for the name *vinutti* (the pushing away). Indeed, he who knows this pushes away his hateful rival.
Of that [sāman], there are two *trivṛt* [stomas] in the middle.
The *trivṛt* is indeed Brahman.
By means of Brahman they drove them away at that time.
He who knows this drives away his hateful rival by means of Brahman alone. 104.
JB 2.105 |va Now they say: "This threefold hymn-form (*trivṛt-stoma*) is indeed Agni.
With two *stomas* of thirty-three [verses] each, which were brought from both sides, they pushed [the Asuras] away.
"They, having retreated, crawled back toward this [earth]," it is said.
Then indeed the gods prevailed, and the Asuras were defeated.
He prospers in himself, and his hateful rival is defeated, for one who knows thus.
Now they say: "One who desires the office of a domestic priest should sacrifice with this [offering] called 'The Overpowering' (*abhibhū*).
On both sides of it there are two *trivṛt* [stomas], and in the middle there are two *trayastrimśa* [stomas].
The *trivṛt* is indeed the *brahman*, and the *trayastrimśa* is the *kṣatra*.
By means of the *brahman* itself, he thus encompasses the *kṣatra* on both sides.
For when he encompasses the *kṣatra* with the *brahman*, then he attains the preeminence of that [kṣatra].
He goes forward; they place him at the front as a domestic priest. Now, moreover, they say: "One should sacrifice with this [offering] when desiring stability, for it is a removal.
Of that [sacrifice], there are two *trivṛt* stomas in the middle, and two *trayastrimśa* stomas on both sides.
The *trivṛt* is indeed the *brahman*, and the *trayastrimśa* is the *kṣatra*.
Thus, by means of the *kṣatra*, he encloses the *brahman* on both sides.
For when he encloses the *brahman* with the *kṣatra*, then the latter remains as its boundary.
It stands within the semi-vowels (*antasthā*), but it is not overcome by the semi-vowels. Furthermore, they say: "Truly, these two *stoma*s are kings, the kings of the *stoma*s.
Now, on both sides of this very Abhibhū [Sāman] there are two *trivṛt* [stomas], and in the middle are two *trayastrimśa* [stomas].
Of these, there are sixty *stotryās*.
Of those, the sixty are the throne (*āsandī*).
Now, those which are the four legs of the throne are [the seasons]. And those two [which remain] are the sacrificer himself; for he is two-legged and is seated upon this royal throne.
He who knows thus attains sovereignty.
“Whether in this world, O Lord, or in that one,” they say; “Furthermore, they say that for whom these two [legs] are tripled at the middle, that indeed is a throne (āsandī).
Or rather, the throne is like something bent in the middle.
|vj This one is, as it were, bent in the middle.
|vk That which is bent in the middle is indeed more hollow.
|vl He who knows this attains sovereignty, whether in this world or in that one.
Now they say: "Verily, these two sacrificial rites are indeed [like] those [two].
Of these two, six stomas rise upwards;
six from there [below] turn downwards. By means of the six, he goes upward to the heavenly world, and he returns from there.
With six [verses] he descends; he goes to the heavenly world and remains in this world. Moreover, he who knows "I am he who was that" is indeed born again in this world.
Furthermore, they say: "He who desires heaven should sacrifice with these two as well."
Now, these two [days] here are together threefold, together fifteenfold, together seventeenfold, together twenty-one-fold, together twenty-seven-fold,
and together thirty-three-fold.
Just as one might proceed by establishing himself with two at a time, even so does he establish himself in the heavenly world by means of these two.
Furthermore, they say: "Verily, these two are the sacrificial rites of the Anviṣṭis."

Whether he has maintained the sacred fires for a year or not, he who would sacrifice with the piling of the fire-altar should sacrifice with these two [oblations]. For him, the year is immediately sought out according to its seasons, months, and half-months.

In that the *stomas* of the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* are employed— the *pṛṣṭhas* being indeed the seasons— and since the year consists of seasons, it is thereby [attained] by means of the seasons. And in that there are twelve *stotras*— the year consisting of twelve months— it is thereby [attained] by means of the months.
Now, as for the fact that there are twenty-four *stotra* and *śastra* hymns: the year consists of twenty-four half-months;
therefore, it is [attained] by half-months.
Indeed, for one who knows this, the year is sought after immediately. 107.
JB 2.108 |va Now follows this Manu-stoma. vb Manu indeed desired: "May I be propagated with abundant offspring and cattle; may I create human progeny."
He saw this sacrifice;
he took it up; with it, he sacrificed.
Then indeed he multiplied through offspring and cattle.
He created these human progeny.
Whoever should desire, "May I multiply through offspring and cattle; may I create human progeny," let him [perform] this.
He should sacrifice.
Verily, he is multiplied with offspring and cattle; he creates human progeny.
These are the *stomas* of that *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*.
The *pṛṣṭha* chants are indeed the seasons;
the seasons are the year;
the year is procreation.
"May he who is procreation cause me to procreate.
For him, both types of *stomas* occur—the odd ones and the even ones.
Indeed, that which consists of both types of *stomas* is a divine pair, a means of procreation.
"May that divine couple, the procreators, procreate me.
For its *stomas* are interwoven; indeed, from an interwoven couple, offspring and cattle are produced—this is for the sake of procreation.
For him, both the Bṛhat and the Rathantara Sāmans are used.
Indeed, these two—the Bṛhat and the Rathantara—are a divine couple, a source of procreation. [He thinks:
"May that which is a divine couple, a source of procreation, cause me to procreate."
Its *pavamāna* stotras are in the *chandomas*.
The *chandomas*, indeed, are cattle;
cattle are procreation.
"May that which is procreative cause me to procreate.
For this [rite], the *mānava* is the *brahmasāman*;
for the *brahmasāman* is indeed the *brahman*.
This *brahmasāman* is the desire of the sacrificer; thus they endow the sacrificer with his desires in his own proper abode. It becomes an *ukthya*.
|vad Prajāpati is indeed offspring and cattle; the *ukthas* are offspring and cattle, for they are procreation.
|vae That which is procreation—may that cause me to procreate. /108/

Now they say, "This is indeed one of the sacrificial rites (*yajñakratu*) of the *anviṣṭis*. Whoever should sacrifice with the piled fire-altar (*agniciti*), whether it has been maintained for a year or not maintained for a year, he should sacrifice with this [rite].
Immediately, indeed, his year becomes sought out according to its seasons, half-months, months, and nights.
Now, as for the fact that the *stomas* of the six-day *pṛṣṭhya* period are used—the *pṛṣṭhas* are indeed the seasons, and the seasons are the year; therefore, it is [sought] according to the seasons.
Now, as for the fact that there are fifteen stotras: there are fifteen nights in a half-month;
therefore, it is [repeated] by half-months.
Now, as for the fact that there are thirty stotras and śastras: there are thirty nights in a month; therefore, it is [repeated] by months.
Now, as there are three hundred and sixty *stotriya* verses, so many are the nights of the year; therefore, it is by way of the nights.
Indeed, for one who knows this, the year is sought out immediately.
Prajāpati desired those [verses], thinking, "May I go to the heavenly world.
He saw this *uttara-manustoma*;
he brought it forth.
With that he sacrificed.
For that *pṛṣṭhya* six-day rite, there are the *stomas*; for the *pṛṣṭhas* are indeed the seasons, and the seasons are the year.

The year is the heavenly world; it serves for the attainment of the heavenly world itself. Its *stomas* are directed upwards; for the heavenly world is indeed directed upwards; it serves for the attainment of the heavenly world itself.
For him, both the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are used; they belong to heaven and serve for the attainment of the heavenly world.
His Pavamāna stotras are in the Chandomas; the Chandomas are indeed cattle, and cattle are the heavenly world; thus it serves for the attainment of the heavenly world.
The *brahmasāman* for this [rite] is the twenty-fifth;
the twenty-fifth is indeed food.
This *brahmasāman* is indeed the desire of the sacrificer.
In its own very abode they thus endow the sacrificer with food.
He becomes one for whom there is the *ukthya* [offering]; for the *ukthas* are indeed offspring and cattle.
Offspring and cattle are indeed the heavenly world; it is for the attainment of the heavenly world itself. 109.
JB 2.110 |va| Now they say: "This is indeed one of the sacrificial rites (*yajñakratu*) of the *anviṣṭi*s.
vb| Therefore, they enter upon that very night.
By means of the Atirātra sacrifice, the gods indeed ascended to the heavenly world.
Having reached the heavenly world, they remained there together, undecided, not knowing the directions. They desired, "May we know the directions."
Beyond day and night, indeed, is the world of heaven.
They saw these four stotras above the night;
with them they praised.
Having praised with those very [verses], they discerned the directions.
Then indeed, wherever they desired of the heavenly world, there they settled. "Wherever one who knows thus desires of the heavenly world, there he settles," so it is said.
Jānaśruteya said:
"Now Vaitahavya indeed said:
'Prajāpati created cattle.'"
Once created from him, they ran away.
He sought to restrain them with the Agniṣṭoma,
but they ran past it.
They sought to hold them back with the Ukthya;
they rushed past that.
They sought to hold them back with the Ṣoḍaśin.
They ran right past him.
He pursued them in turn. Because he pursued them in turn, that is the reason for the "turns" (paryāya) of the paryāyas.
He encompassed them with the Aśvina sacrifice. Of those thus encompassed, just as small fish might slip through the gaps of a net, even so those small animals that were there slipped away.
He desired them, thinking, "May I obtain them and hold them within myself.
He saw these four stotras after the night; with them he praised.
Having reached them with those very [verses], he drew them into himself.

Because he drew them into himself after reaching them, therefore it is called the *aptoryāma*. Furthermore, because he followed along, manifesting the *soma* as if it were something to be reached (*āptu*), for that reason also it is the *aptoryāma*. (110)
JB 2.111 |va These amount to sixty-two *stotriya* verses.
vb Of these, the sixty constitute the *virāj*.
The cattle are the Virāj.
Now, those two [verses] are the sacrificer himself; he is thus established as a biped beyond [the cattle].
It is for the protection of the cattle, for the non-loss of the cattle.

The wealth of one who knows thus is not diminished. Furthermore, they say: "This is indeed a single *stotra*, but having spread it out fourfold, one should chant it—six verses for the Hotṛ, six for the Maitrāvaruṇa, six for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and six for the Acchāvāka."
The Hotṛ alone should recite that;
thus they amount to twenty-four stotriya verses. There are twenty-four half-months in a year.
Prajāpati is the year;
he is indeed Prajāpati himself, raised up on the far side,
for the protection of cattle and so that cattle may not be lost.
The wealth of one who knows this is not diminished.
Regarding this, they say: "The Trivṛt, the Pañcadaśa, the Saptadaśa, and the Ekaviṃśa—these indeed should be the Stotras.
For all sacrificial rites (yajñakratu) conclude according to the Ekaviṃśa.
Now, this twenty-one-fold hymn-form (*stoma*) is indeed firm and well-established;
therefore, the twenty-one-fold hymn-form alone should be employed at the conclusion. Regarding this, they say: "They should follow [the ritual] with the forms of the *pṛṣṭha* chants. 111.
"abhi tvā vṛṣabhā suta" is the [sūkta] belonging to the bull;
"abhi" is the form of the Rathantara.
Therefore, they do not depart from the form of the Rathantara.
"Whatever [deeds] today, O slayer of Vṛtra..."—this Śākala verse, containing the *hiṃ* syllable, is the form of the Vāmadevya;
therefore, they do not depart from the form of the Vāmadevya.
"O Indra, we strengthen you"—this has *edāvasu* as its finale (*nidhana*) and *bahiḥ* as its finale; it is the form of the *Bṛhat*.
By means of this, they do not depart from the form of the *Bṛhat*. Moreover, wealth (*vasu*) is indeed cattle; it is for the attainment of cattle.
Furthermore, having reached them with the thought, "This is wealth," he approaches them. "Viṣṇu strode through this"—this is the *iḍānām*.
The *iḍā* is indeed a mixture of cattle; it is for the attainment of cattle.
For this reason, they offered these [verses] to them, saying, "Come, O *iḍā*! Come, O *iḍā*! Since the *iḍā* is cattle, therefore these *atiriktoktha*s (additional hymns) should be performed.
Regarding this, Tāṇḍya said: Prajāpati created cattle;
once they were created, they departed from him.
He said to Agni, "Keep these away from me."
He did not ward them off with the *jarābodhīya* [sāman].
He said to Indra, "Do you ward these off for me?
He did not ward them off with the *satrāsāhīya* [sāman].
He said to the god Īśāna, "Ward these off for me.
He did not ward them off with the *mārgīyava* [plant].
He said to Viṣṇu, "Ward these off for me."
He indeed warded them off with the Vāravantīya chant upon the Vaiṣṇava verses. Because he warded them off (*avārayata*), that is the reason for the name *vāravantīya*.
Therefore, these [chants] must certainly be performed as *atiriktoktha* (excess hymns). 112.
JB 2.113 |va Now follows this Gosava sacrifice. vb One who desires heaven should indeed sacrifice with this.
This [stoma], indeed, consists of thirty-six [syllables].
The *bṛhatī* consists of thirty-six syllables;
the *bṛhatī* is the heavenly world, the sovereign rule (*sāmrājya*).
Thus, they proceed establishing themselves in the *bṛhatī* metre, in the heavenly world, and in sovereign rule.

Indeed, the *bṛhatī* pervades all these worlds by means of its syllables: it pervades this world with ten syllables, the intermediate space with ten, that [heavenly] world with ten, the quarters with four, and the two [worlds above and below] with two.
Day and night.
He [performed it] with the thought: "She pervades these worlds; may I, through her, pervade these worlds.
For him, each stotra becomes four times threefold.
Other *stomas* resolve into the *trivṛt*, and the *trivṛt* [resolves into] the heavenly world.
Just as one would go wherever one wishes to go by means of a swift horse harnessed to a four-horse chariot, even so does one go to the heavenly world by means of this.
For him, both the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans are employed; they belong to heaven for the attainment of the heavenly world.
It is an Ukthya sacrifice; the Ukthas are indeed offspring and cattle, and offspring and cattle are the heavenly world—for the attainment of the heavenly world itself.
Twelve thousand [cows] are his sacrificial fee; twelve months are a year, and the year is the heavenly world—for the attainment of the heavenly world itself. His vow is...
He should approach his mother, his sister, or a woman of the same lineage.
Having approached, he should sip water; having approached, he should pluck blades of grass.
Wherever he may find excrement, there he should void it.
One indeed wins the world of the oxen.
With this very [sacrifice], Janaka of Videha performed a sacrifice.
The Brahmins sat down all around him.
He asked: "What is the *stoma*?
He [Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi] replied: "This is not merely the *trivṛt*, so they say.
[The other asked: "What is its vow? What is its sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*)?"
He told this to him. He said:
"I indeed hoped for his sacrificial fees, but I did not hope for his vow. Because of that, he did not dare to sacrifice.
Therefore, Puṇyakeśa Yaudheni, King Śaibya, performed a sacrifice.
While he was seated in the assembly hall, Viṣṭha found him. Turning back toward him, he said: "This man was indeed a performer of sacrifices for the elderly."
Only an elder (*sthavira*) should perform this sacrifice; for all of this is indeed authorized for an elder. This, then, is the sacrifice of the elder.
Therefore, one should perform this very sacrifice only in the latter part of life.
Now follows this Vivadha sacrifice.
One who desires cattle should sacrifice with this.
Indeed, it consists of six *paṅkti* verses and ten *stotriya* verses.
Of these, the six *paṅkti* verses are cattle.
Now, those ten *stotryā* verses are indeed the milking of cattle;
that is their milk.
Furthermore, those two [sets of] five each become two *pañktis*, consisting of five [syllables] each.
And those are indeed the animals. Its morning pressing consists of twenty [stotras], its midday pressing consists of twenty,
and its third pressing consists of twenty.
Just as, indeed, the two ends of a cross-bar are provided with knobs for the sake of its being a cross-bar,
so it is that the midday pressing has a fringe.
On both sides, in the front half and the rear half, they cause it to receive the largest share, [namely] twenty [stotras].

Therefore, cattle provide the greatest portion with both the forepart and the hindpart. They carry [the load] with the forepart and yield milk with the hindpart; they bring forth offspring from the hindpart.
He who knows this obtains both the milk of the cow and the milk of the ox.
At that time, they should perform both the Bṛhat and the Rathantara [Sāmans]. Indeed, cattle are of two kinds:
some belong to the Rathantara, others to the Bṛhat. Those cattle that have teeth on only one side are of the Rathantara type; those that have teeth on both sides are of the Bṛhat type.

It is for the attainment of both kinds of cattle. It is an Ukthya sacrifice; the Ukthas are indeed cattle, [and it is] for the attainment of cattle. Its Acchāvāka-sāman is the Udvamśīya, which is the form of all the Pṛṣṭhas; for cattle are indeed the Pṛṣṭhas.
This is for the sake of securing cattle that have been previously seized.
Now follows this Sadyaḥkrī purchase.

Being thus chosen, they did not depart. They came and performed the sacrifice for them. For them, they brought this speech, which had become a white mare, harnessed to the yoke-halter of a horse. This [is she].
"Accept me!
they said. They replied, "She is superior to us; we shall not lift her up. Enraged, thinking, "They did not accept me," she became a lioness with faces on both sides and leapt upwards into the water.
She stood between the gods and the asuras, beautifying them; whichever of the gods she reached and whichever of the asuras she reached,
taking hold of that [portion], ||| the gods indeed took counsel regarding her, and so did the asuras.
She, returning toward the gods, said: "What would accrue to me from this, that I should return to you? [They replied:
"May the first oblation reach you before Agni.
They assigned her a place in the sacrifice.
This is the high altar (uttaravedi).
The first oblation to Agni reaches it.
They maintain the fire; they establish the high altar (*uttaravedi*).
Thus, this first oblation reaches her from the fire.
Then, for these [deities], the Ādityas [offer] this horse, which has become white, bound with horse-hair thongs.
"Bring him here, and indeed, let us accept him! they said. They replied, "He is certainly superior to us; we shall not lift him up.
Then the gods and the seers approached them and said, "The sacrifices will surely be cut off if they are without sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*)."
"Accept it!
Thus it is recited in reference to this:
"O singer, the Ādityas brought the horse as a sacrificial fee to the Aṅgirases."
"O singer, they did not recognize him; O singer, they did not accept him.
But them, O singer, they recognized; them, O singer, they accepted, [thinking]: 'Let there not be days without a leader, let there not be sacrifices without consciousness.'"
"O Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, rejoice in this; O Aṅgiras, accept this gift!
O gods, grant us this great and wide boon!"
"May that be well-intentioned for you," [he said];
"may it be with you day by day;
grasp it indeed!"—in this way he caused them to accept it.
Then, indeed, the Ādityas first went to the heavenly world, while the Aṅgirases were left behind.
He who has rivals, he who would practice sorcery, or he who would compete, should sacrifice with this [rite].
His evil is cast away, his rival departs, and he goes to the heavenly world.
The sacrificial altar (vedi) consists of barley soil;
for it has been prepared beforehand,
and the high-altar (uttaravedi) is made of barley.
The Ādityas won over the sacrifice of the Aṅgirases with barley. Because they won over the sacrifice with barley, that is the reason for the name of barley (*yava*).
With barley alone, he wins over the sacrifice of his hateful rival.
The sacrificial post is made of *khadira* wood; its top is like a wooden sword (*sphya*), for it belongs to Indra.
They immolate the animals together for victory and for completeness.
The Soma-purchasing ox is a male; the male is indeed vigor, [thinking] "May we be full of vigor."
It is a castrated bull, for the sake of [attaining] the state of Indra. The *vasatīvarī* waters are taken from a jar from the houses of one who has been born before;
for they have indeed already been drawn previously.
Having eaten food with clarified butter, he lies down.
That very *dīkṣaṇīya* offering which he eats becomes for him that which has been eaten.
He lies between the thighs of his beloved wife, not lying down [on a bed].
Having placed that very austerity as his gold upon his mouth, he lies down.
Gold is indeed truth; thus, truth itself becomes manifest for him. 117.

A white horse is the sacrificial fee; for the horse is heavenly, and it serves for the attainment of the heavenly world. The chariot-horse is the announcer of the Soma, its maximum distance being a yojana.

Indeed, among the highest distances, the *yojana* is the shortest; or, among the shortest, it is the longest. In that [distance], a leather bag filled with curd is placed. Whatever clarified butter (*sarpiḥ*) drips from it, they pour into the jar of sacrificial ghee (*ājya*).

For that [sacrificial ground], like one just born, extends for two *krośas* in this manner, and the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) are stationed in this manner at intervals of two *krośas*. They approach him in the morning and perform the sacrifice for him.
While offering the oblation, he closes his eyes three times and looks out three times.
Those very [days] are the consecration (dīkṣā) and the preparatory days (upasada).
He [the sacrifice] is the Trivṛt-stoma with the Rathantara-sāman; the Trivṛt is indeed the Brahman.
"The *brahman* is the *rathantara*; through the *brahman*, let us go to the heavenly world," they say. Furthermore, they say that the *bṛhat-sāman* should indeed be the *trivṛt*.
The *trivṛt* is the *brahman*, and the *bṛhat* is the *kṣatra*.
"By means of both the *brahman* and the *kṣatra*, joined together, may we go to the heavenly world.
Regarding this, they say: "The *rathaṃtara-sāman* should indeed be the *trivṛt*;
for the *trivṛt* is the *brahman*."
The *rathaṃtara* is indeed the *brahman*.
The *brahman* rules over the heavenly world. Therefore, in that [rite], the *rathaṃtara-sāman* should indeed be the *trivṛt*.
Regarding that, they say: "So many *sāmans* should be performed; for by means of so many [verses], the gods went to the heavenly world;
'by means of so many, may we go to the heavenly world.
Furthermore, they say: "Those *sāmans* which have the fire as their source (*agniyoni*)—those indeed should be performed."
This [sacrifice] which is performed on the same day is, as it were, uncooked;
for Agni is the cooker of what is uncooked.
Regarding this, they also say: "The [Sāmans] should indeed be those of the Agniṣṭoma."
These Agniṣṭoma-sāmans are indeed the wombs of Agni;
therefore, the Agniṣṭoma-sāmans alone should be performed.
Now, this [path] leads more swiftly from swift, more swiftly from swift, to heaven.
"Let us go to the world.
It has twelve stotras; there are twelve months in a year, and the year is the heavenly world. This is for the attainment of the heavenly world itself.
It has twenty-four *stotra-śastras*; the year consists of twenty-four half-months; the year is the heavenly world, for the attainment of the heavenly world itself. 119.
Now, these two are to be performed in succession.
The Ādityas and the Aṅgirases once contended for the world of heaven.
Those Ādityas went first to the world of heaven.
Those Aṅgirasas desired, "May we too go to that world which the Ādityas have gone to.
They saw this sacrifice;
though it already existed, they brought it forth by means of the indirect method.
They sacrificed with that. Having led a white mare as the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), they became co-residents (*saloka*) with the Ādityas.
These, then, are the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases who are co-residents.
He who knows thus indeed dwells in the same world as the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases.
Moreover, they say that he for whom a kinsman is superior should sacrifice with this [rite]. For he who is superior is like one who has already departed before.
By this, they reached those [ancestors] as if they were the deceased of old;
having reached a superior [state], he becomes better off in himself. 120.
The altar-ground consists of wheat;
for it has been prepared beforehand.
The high-altar (uttaravedi) is made of wheat for the sake of secrecy.
The sacrificial post is made of *khalevalā* wood with a top like a wooden sword; it belongs to Indra for the sake of victory. They immolate the animals together for the sake of attainment.
The female cow used for purchasing Soma is of a different color for the sake of concealment.
The *vasatīvarī* waters are contained in a jar; they are taken from the house of one who is already born [in the lineage]. For they have been previously drawn.
Having eaten food mixed with clarified butter, he lies down.
That very *dīkṣaṇīya* [oblation] which he eats, that indeed becomes eaten by him.
He lies between the thighs of his beloved wife, not sitting down.
Having placed that gold, which is his asceticism (*tapas*), upon his face, he lies there.
Gold is indeed truth;
thus, truth itself is declared for him.
It is silver for the sake of concealment.

A white mare is the sacrificial fee for the sake of indirectness. The chariot drawn by mules belongs to the *somapravāka* for the sake of indirectness; it has three tracks as its highest point for the sake of indirectness.
Upon it, a leather bag filled with curds is placed.
Whatever clarified butter (*sarpiṣ*) drips from it, they pour into the jar of sacrificial ghee (*ājyakuṃbha*).

For that [ghee] is as if freshly produced; at a distance of one and a half *krośas*, the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) are stationed at intervals of one and a half *krośas*. They approach him in the morning and perform the sacrifice for him.
While offering the oblation, he closes his eyes three times and looks three times.
Those very [acts] constitute the consecration (dīkṣā) and the Upasad rites.
Indeed, this [sacrifice] consists of eighteen Pavamāna chants.
The Trivṛt is indirect. The Ādityas are performers of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, while the Aṅgirases are performers of the Ukthya sacrifice.
This very Ukthya, being established as its underlying principle, is brought back as the Agniṣṭoma for the sake of swiftness.
Now, this [sacrifice] consists of twenty-four *pavamāna* stotras;
yet, in a hidden sense, it is indeed the *trivṛt*.
This very *atirātra*, being established by its fundamental principle (*nidāna*), is either a *ṣoḍaśin* or an *agniṣṭoma* that is brought back for the sake of swiftness.
Now follows this *parikrī*.
Khaṇḍika Auddhāri and Keśin Dārbhya were competing against each other among the Pañcālas.
Khaṇḍika sent for Keśin,
saying, "He is indeed going to perform a sacrifice immediately."
Now, having proclaimed it by means of this [rite], they perform sacrifices for their rivals.
Of him, these were the Brāhmaṇas who were Ahīnas: Āśvatthi, Keśin Sātyakāmi, Gaṅgin Rāhakṣita, and Luśākapi Khārgali.
They approached him;
he sat down reflecting;
they said to him, "Why does the king reflect?"
He said, "Indeed, I have nothing to meditate upon. [The same expression occurs at 2.100 (201,16f.
"You, O Brahmins, recite! The Ādityas and the Aṅgirases were competing for the heavenly world.
Those Ādityas first went to the heavenly world; the Aṅgirases were left behind."
He who, having announced it with this [formula], performs the sacrifice for his rival, he alone prospers; his hateful rival is defeated.
“Khaṇḍika indeed intended that for him; he will surely perform the sacrifice tomorrow,” [said Māyu]. “He will surely be defeated; I am thinking just this:
‘He will be surpassed,’” [said Khaṇḍika]. They said to him, “This sacrificial rite is indeed called ‘the purchase’ (parikrī).”
"Let us have you perform the sacrifice for us," they said.
"So be it," he replied.
And so, they had him perform the sacrifice.
Now, they chant each verse of this very *ṛc*-trio one by one.
The first *stotriyā* is indeed the *brahman*, the second is the *kṣatra*, and the third is the *viś*.
For the *kṣatra* and the *viś* are indeed supported by the *brahman*.
The realm of the *kṣatriya* and the realm of the *viś* follow upon the world of the enemy. When he cut off two [verses], he thereby cut off the world of the enemy.
The first *stotriyā* is indeed the self; the second is the wife; the third is the offspring.

Indeed, one's wife and offspring are the very support of oneself; and following upon the wife and offspring, there is the world of the enemy. When he cut off two [of his ribs], he thereby cut off the world of the enemy. 123.
JB 2.124 |va Then indeed he caused Khaṇḍika to be expelled.
vb Thereupon Keśin became the ruler of the Dārbhyas, while Khaṇḍika was defeated.
He prospers by himself, and his hateful rival is defeated—he who knows thus.
For him, the *bahiṣpavamāna* is performed on three verses; the *ājya* stotras on four; the midday *pavamāna* on five;
the *pṛṣṭha* stotras on four; the *ārbhava-pavamāna* on seven; and the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* on one.
These amount to twenty-four stotriyas.
There are twenty-four half-months in a year.
It was from the year itself that Keśin Dārbhya pushed away the Khaṇḍika Audbhāri; it was from the year...
For the sake of separation:
he who knows thus repels his hateful rival within a year; he separates himself from him within a year.
JB 2.125 |va Now follows this Ekatrika sacrifice. vb One who desires offspring should perform it with this.
Prajāpati indeed desired: "May I be multiplied through offspring and cattle; may I pervade this expansion.
He beheld this sacrifice.
He brought it; he sacrificed with it.
He reflected: "With what shall I praise?"
He saw himself. He praised with that. He reflected: "By what, indeed, shall I praise?
He saw the out-breath, the in-breath, and the diffused breath.
They praised him.

He, together with himself, together with the out-breath, the in-breath, and the diffused breath; he, together with himself, together with the out-breath, the in-breath, and the diffused breath—thus indeed did he complete the sacrifice in reverse order.
Then indeed he multiplied through offspring and cattle; he attained this distinction which is his.
He who knows thus multiplies through offspring and cattle and attains this distinction. 125.
JB 2.126 |va With this very [sacrifice], Udara Śāṇḍilya desired to sacrifice. vb He had the thought in his mind: "I shall sacrifice with the Ekatrika."
But he did not say anything at all to anyone.
Now his wife was possessed by a Gandharva; that Gandharva came and approached her.
He said to her, "The sacrificial ritual (*yajñakratu*) called the *ekatrika* is indeed as if harsh. By means of it, your husband will sacrifice.
She then asked her husband, "The sacrificial ritual called the *ekatrika* is indeed as if harsh."
"Is it true that you will sacrifice with that yakṣa?
He replied, "Since I have not told this to anyone at all here, it was only in my mind; who has told this to you?"
“Who is this Gandharva who approaches me? he asked.
“Ask him yourself,” he replied. “Is the sacrifice to be performed by him, or is it not to be performed? he asked.
He asked him: "Is he to be sacrificed with, or is he not to be sacrificed with?
He replied: "Just as he knows him, so do we know him.
But whoever should know his stotra in this manner, he should sacrifice with him—just as Prajāpati praised him with it here."
Therefore, he did not dare to sacrifice. Indeed, Uddālaka Śāṇḍilya always attained that which was worthy of praise because it was present in his mind.
"One should sacrifice with the *ekatrika* [stoma]," it is said.
Indeed, this sacrifice is, as it were, one-sided; having sacrificed with it, one becomes either very prosperous or very wretched.
For that [sacrifice], the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is completed in a single [verse]: "Sing forth to him, O men! (*upāsmai gāyatā nara*).
In the three [verses], the Mādhyandina-pavamāna is in the Gāyatrī meter: the *utsedha* in the Gāyatrī, the *satobṛhatī* in which is the *iḍā*, and the *āuśana* as the *nidhana*.
In the Triṣṭubh meters, it is the Ārbhava-pavamāna, beginning with "ayā rucā hariṇyā punānaḥ."
In this *aticchandas* [verse], there is the *gāyatrapārśva* [chant]. That same *svara* [is used], with that as the *nidhana*.
It consists of seven feet.
There are indeed seven meters. The *aticchandas* (exceeding meter) indeed overcomes all the meters;
thus, for him, all the meters become attained.
Regarding this, they say: "The Vāmadevya [Sāman] should indeed be performed with five *nidhanas*.
The *Ārbhava-pavamāna* consists of five meters and seven *sāmans*.
Since there are five *nidhanas*, by that means it corresponds to the meters."
Because it is indeed seven-footed, it manifests here as the *sāman*.
Regarding this, they say: it should be made with the *gāyatra* on one side; that itself is the *svara*, and that is the *nidhana*.
The self is indeed the *svara*, and offspring are the *nidhana*.
This very [form] with the *gāyatra* on the sides is, as it were, more complete.
Therefore, one should perform it specifically with the *gāyatra* on the sides.
These amount to twenty-four stotriyas.
There are twenty-four half-months in a year;
the year is procreation.
"May he who is procreation cause me to procreate," [he says].
Now, this is the Bṛhaspatisava.
Prajāpati, while creating offspring, became exhausted. Having become food, he lay down.
All the gods were intent on possessing him, thinking, "It is mine! It is mine!"
They said, "Let us divide this. In dividing it, they could not reach an agreement.
They said, "Let us compete for it in a race."
They went to that battle.
Bṛhaspati saw a path leading to the front of the battle;
having gone around first by means of his chariot, he stood there, having chosen [his position].
Those gods did not find that by which they might have crossed over. Indeed, for as long as there was space for a chariot to travel, so long was the race-course.
Thereupon, he won that race.
Because Bṛhaspati won [the prize], it is therefore called the Bṛhaspatisava.
To him, having won that race, Indra said: "I place you in front;
let me officiate for you with this sacrifice."
"So be it," he said. He placed him in front and caused him to sacrifice with him.
Then indeed Indra attained preeminence among all the gods;
he who knows thus attains preeminence among his own people.
This sacrifice, indeed, belongs to only two: the Brāhmaṇa and the Rājanya.
Because Bṛhaspati won by means of the *atirikta* (extra) [offering], it belongs to the Brāhmaṇa;
because Indra sacrificed, it belongs to the Rājanya.
And he alone was the domestic priest (*purohita*) for Indra, not for the other gods.
He desired, "May I attain the position of priest for all the gods.
He sacrificed with this very sacrifice. Thereupon, he indeed attained the position of priest for all the gods.
Bṛhaspati is indeed the domestic priest (purohita) of the gods.
He is the one who possesses the *trivṛt* [stoma] and has the *rathantara* as his *sāman*.
The *trivṛt* is indeed Brahman; the *rathantara* is Brahman.
By means of Brahman, he indeed attained that splendor of Brahman (*brahmavarcasa*).
He who knows thus attains the splendor of Brahman through Brahman alone.
There are thirty-three sacrificial fees for it;
for there are indeed thirty-three deities;
thus he attains the pre-eminence among the deities.
The horse is the thirty-fourth [syllable].
(vi) Now, the horse is indeed the form of Prajāpati.
(vj) By means of it, he attains the preeminence among the deities together with Prajāpati.

To him he gives these sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās) at each pressing according to the preceding rule: he gives eight at the morning pressing, eleven at the midday pressing, twelve at the third pressing; one at the Anūbandhyā sacrifice, and one at the Udavasānīyā sacrifice.
At each pressing, he gives the horse in three parts.

Now, those eight which he gives at the morning pressing—thereby he attains the pre-eminence of the Vasus, for there are eight Vasus. Then those eleven which he gives at the midday pressing—thereby he attains the pre-eminence of the Rudras, for there are eleven Rudras.
He attained the pre-eminence of the Vasus.

Then, those twelve [cups] at the third pressing—thereby he attained the pre-eminence of the twelve Ādityas among the Ādityas. And that one [cup] at the Anūbandhyā sacrifice—thereby he attained the pre-eminence of Mitra and Varuṇa.

Now, that one [offering] which he performs at the *udavasānīyā* sacrifice with the thought, "May my ritual action be accompanied by a sacrificial fee," and then that horse which he offers at each pressing in three parts— by means of that very [act], he attained the office of domestic priest for Prajāpati.
Regarding this, they say: "One should give at the morning pressing with the mind alone, and at the third pressing with the mind alone; one should give only at the midday pressing.
On this point, however, they also say: "The morning pressing is indeed not a proper crossing-point for sacrificial gifts, and the third pressing is not a proper crossing-point for sacrificial gifts."
One should give [the gift] at the midday pressing alone;
that indeed is the proper time, that is the proper place.
One should not, even in thought, pay heed to giving at the other two pressings.
He gives the horse to the Brahman priest;
for the Brahman’s fee is indeed singular.
Then, when the cups of the midday pressing have been set down, he [should go] behind the Āhavanīya fire.

He should say, "Spread out the black antelope skin with its neck pointing eastward, or with its neck pointing northward. Then the sacrificer sits down and wipes the cups that have been offered, [saying]: "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, for Sarasvatī thee, with the restraint of Vāc, the restrainer."
"O Bṛhaspati, I consecrate you with sovereignty and with the sacred word (brahman). Having said this, he wipes his face.
